Approved evidence

Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks

paper.arxiv.2503.14499

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Complete pinned v4 primary manuscript read separately by three AI invocations; all approved claims bind exact actual author, source-verifier and adversarial source-content review digests. Composite HCAST/RE-Bench/SWAA input scopes, human-time versus agent duration, logistic weighting/uncertainty, historical trend and forecast/scaffold limits remain qualified. The original overbroad human-time-calibration hypothesis remains a candidate with its genuine original source-verifier REVISE and actual author/adversarial records; its separately reviewed corrected successor scopes the geometric mean rule to HCAST and preserves RE-Bench fixed eight-hour treatment. No original negative is overwritten, no fresh performance or reproduction claimed, and core eligibility remains unfrozen.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks · documents: The paper reports approximately eight attempts per agent/task pair and uses general agent scaffolds without task-specific prompting, except that SWAA uses a simple prompting scaffold.

candidate.next8.metr.paper.agent-execution-conditions.v1

  • The run count is approximate because some runs failed from internal infrastructure issues.
  • Most listed models use modular-public; o1 uses triframe and o1-preview uses duet.
  • GPT-2 receives imputed zero scores on HCAST and RE-Bench because its context length is incompatible with the scaffold.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks · evaluates: For the reported 2019–2025 model series, the paper estimates a 207-day doubling time with a 95% bootstrapped interval of 166–240 days, using 10,000 resamples over task groups, tasks and runs.

candidate.next8.metr.paper.historical-trend-and-bootstrap.v1

  • Uncertainty in individual model horizons is correlated because resampling easier or harder tasks affects multiple models together.
  • For unavailable original GPT-3 and GPT-3.5 variants, the analysis assigns the earlier release dates to available substitute models described in the paper.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks · paper method: For HCAST, task durations are calculated using the geometric mean time of successful human baseline attempts, with manual estimates for tasks lacking successful baselines; RE-Bench instead receives a fixed eight-hour duration rating.

candidate.next8.metr.paper.human-time-calibration.v2

  • The paper cautions that conditioning on success and incentives to give up early can bias task-time ratings, particularly for longer tasks.
  • HCAST and RE-Bench use external contractors, whereas SWAA uses internal employees and a custom short-task timing interface.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks · paper method: The method fits an agent-specific logistic model against log human task duration; the fitted horizon is the duration with predicted 50% success, and each task receives weight equal to the inverse square root of its task-group size.

  • Human difficulty is supplied from baseline durations rather than learned jointly from agent responses, and the fitted slope varies by agent.
